papers.title: Secrets in Preamble: Practical and Robust PHY Information Hiding for Wi-Fi
papers.abstract: Physical layer (PHY) information hiding refers to the concealment of secrets within PHY waveforms without compromising the integrity of the primary communication link, thereby enabling critical applications such as covert communication, PHY steganography, and watermarking. The widespread deployment of Wi-Fi has motivated substantial research interest in hiding secrets within Wi-Fi waveforms. However, existing Wi-Fi information hiding approaches suffer from two limitations: restricted steganographic capacity and insufficient robustness against environmental variations, both of which severely constrain practical deployment. This work proposes to embed secrets within the Wi-Fi legacy short training field (L-STF). The designed method preserves the autocorrelation properties of Wi-Fi L-STF, ensuring that packet detection and coarse frequency offset compensation functionalities remain uncompromised. The secret embedding and extraction processes employ a pair of neural networks designed to learn optimal embedding rules and maximize steganographic capacity. We developed a prototype system and conducted comprehensive experiments across both indoor and outdoor environments. Experimental results show that our method can reliably embed 46 secret bits within Wi-Fi packets across diverse channel conditions, achieving significantly enhanced steganographic capacity and environmental robustness. The hardware prototype study validates the feasibility of the proposed Wi-Fi information hiding scheme.

papers.title: Stochastic Finite-Transition Learning and Exploration for Accelerated MRI Reconstruction
papers.abstract: Generative MRI reconstruction maps an initial source distribution to the target image distribution along a learned recovery trajectory. Common generative methods, such as diffusion and flow, typically learn fine-grained local dynamics whose integration defines this global mapping, hence requiring many network evaluations at inference. Existing few-step sampling approaches can lower computational burden by approximating large transformations from local dynamics, albeit at the expense of reconstruction fidelity. FLEX-MRI instead partitions recovery into a small number of finite intervals between retained states defined by progressive changes in k-space support, and directly learns the reconstruction change across each interval. Because such finite transitions can admit multiple plausible outcomes, FLEX-MRI combines support-relaxed finite-transition learning with stochastic exploration. During training, randomized k-space sampling masks define finite-transition targets with varying support, while the prediction loss remains unrestricted by each individual mask. At inference, FLEX-MRI perturbs a random subset of currently estimated k-space coefficients, allowing the learned predictor to stochastically explore alternative transition paths. Each predicted state is then reconciled with the acquired measurements through data consistency. We theoretically show that this stochastic exploration induces nonzero transition-level variation through the learned recovery map and data consistency without requiring an auxiliary generative sampler. Experiments on multi-coil MRI datasets show that FLEX-MRI outperforms competing methods while maintaining computational efficiency comparable to few-step baselines.

papers.title: ECGWmark: Deep Watermarking for Electrocardiogram Signals
papers.abstract: Secure transmission of electrocardiogram (ECG) signals remains a major challenge in telecardiology. While traditional mathematical watermarking can embed patient metadata directly into ECG signals, it is highly fragile against temporal desynchronization such as circular phase shifts. In contrast, existing deep watermarking approaches for temporal signals, such as audio, typically rely on lossy quantization, which compromises the high-frequency micro-morphological details critical for clinical diagnosis. To bridge this gap, we propose ECGWmark, a fully convolutional and quantization-free deep watermarking framework for medical time-series. ECGWmark operates in a continuous, full-resolution latent space and utilizes a localized frame-level mechanism to improve the robustness to severe desynchronization. Crucially, we introduce a differentiable Physiological Loss guided by a clinical classifier to preserve diagnostic semantics. Experiments on the benchmark MIT-BIH database show that ECGWmark maintains channel-bit extraction accuracy above 90% under the evaluated circular temporal shifts. Furthermore, under a rigorous inter-patient diagnostic evaluation, Class-V sensitivity changes from 71.97% to 76.50%, whereas Macro-F1 changes from 35.25% to 34.71% and Class-S sensitivity from 8.89% to 1.39%; these results indicate mixed class-level effects.

papers.title: CNN-Transformer with Sigmoid Label for High-Resolution Sub-Degree DOA Estimation
papers.abstract: This paper addresses the grid quantization error of deep-learning (DL)-based direction-of-arrival (DOA) estimation. Classification- based DOA methods discretize the continuous angular space into a grid, so that with a peak-based read-out, the accuracy and resolution are limited by the grid step and by the width of the label peak. To address this issue, we propose a sigmoid label that encodes the sources' DOAs as the sum of angle-shifted monotonic sigmoid functions. Differentiating the output of a CNN-Transformer network trained with the sigmoid label produces sharp spectral peaks at the source DOAs. Combined with a moderately refined grid step of 0.25 degrees, the CNN-Transformer with the proposed sigmoid label attains sub-degree accuracy and a 1-degree resolution, breaking the limit of the grid quantization error. Under the unified CNN-Transformer backbone, we compare the proposed Sigmoid label with the Gaussian label, the 0-1 hard label, and the binary cross-entropy (BCE) baseline. Numerical results demonstrate that the Sigmoid label attains the highest accuracy and superior resolution compared to other labels.

papers.title: OpenPA: Forced-alignment-free Multi-granular Pronunciation Assessment with Mixed-transcript Adaptation
papers.abstract: Recent advances in automatic pronunciation assessment (APA) have driven a shift from scripted to free-form assessment. However, existing methods often rely on multi-stage pipelines with forced alignment and separate feature extractors, limiting their practicality across response settings. In light of this, we propose OpenPA, a novel APA framework that leverages Whisper's cross-attention mechanism to jointly predict word- and utterance-level pronunciation scores without forced alignment. Through mixed-transcript adaptation and adaptive substitution weighting, OpenPA accommodates heterogeneous transcripts across closed- and open-response settings within a single model. Trained solely on speechocean762, OpenPA achieves the strongest overall performance among evaluated systems under in-domain closed and simulated open-response conditions, while maintaining its performance zero-shot on MultiPA. An additional cross-task evaluation on oral-cancer speech suggests its potential applicability beyond non-native speech.

papers.title: A Multi-Scenario UAV RF Dataset with Real-World Acquisition and Signal Processing Benchmarking
papers.abstract: We present a real-world multi-scenario unmanned aerial vehicle (UAV) radio frequency (RF) dataset, namely DRFF-R2, which is collected using a dedicated acquisition platform under diverse operational conditions. All signals are acquired within a unified framework to ensure consistency in hardware configuration and environmental settings. The dataset is systematically organized into seven well-defined subsets corresponding to different operational and signal composition scenarios to facilitate structured experimentation. Each file follows a clearly annotated naming convention to enable convenient data indexing and reproducible analysis. The dataset contains RF recordings from 26 UAV units spanning 8 distinct models, captured across varying flight states, altitudes, speeds, acquisition days, and receiver configurations. By covering diverse acquisition settings and signal compositions, the dataset provides a comprehensive resource for future UAV RF signal research, including RF fingerprinting (RFF) identification, model-level recognition, flight state analysis, time-varying RFF study, and interference-aware signal processing.

papers.title: ThinkNet: Evolutionary Deep Ensembles for Efficient Motor-Imagery EEG Classification
papers.abstract: Practical assistive and rehabilitative brain--computer interfaces require subject-independent motor-imagery EEG (MI-EEG) decoders that generalize to new users under limited target-user data and constrained compute. However, held-out-subject performance can be overstated when test-subject information influences preprocessing, model selection, or ensemble selection. We present \textit{ThinkNet}, a validation-controlled framework that combines train-only normalization, validation-guided evolutionary search, and validation-gated inference to identify compact decoders and inference policies for held-out subjects. We evaluate four-class BCI Competition IV-2a (session T) decoding with nine Leave-One-Subject-Out (LOSO) folds, three seeds, seven fixed decoder entries, and a broader search over ten representative decoder families; the held-out subject is never used for normalization, hyperparameter, architecture, or ensemble-policy selection. In the fixed benchmark, the validation-selected compact decoder achieved 44.35$\pm$15.41\% accuracy with 4.9K parameters, 19 KB FP32 weights, and 0.99 ms batch-1 Orin CUDA inference. Across the broader search, compact models ($\leq$25K parameters) achieved higher mean held-out accuracy than mid-size and large alternatives after selected retraining (40.10\% vs. 35.09\% and 34.78\%). Validation-gated ensembling improved over validation-selected single-model inference, reaching 43.98$\pm$16.25\% in the fixed benchmark and 43.31$\pm$15.88\% for the compact six-family ensemble. A non-deployable oracle analysis revealed a 6.1-point family-selection gap and near-zero validation--test correlation, showing that validation reliability remains a key bottleneck under subject shift. Thus, ThinkNet is a validation-controlled framework for compact MI-EEG model and inference-policy selection, rather than a single-architecture benchmark.

papers.title: Expert-level detection of low-voltage intervals in EEG as a robust biomarker of neonatal encephalopathy
papers.abstract: Background: Discontinuity in neonatal EEG is a critical marker of brain dysfunction but can be difficult to quantify visually. Inter-burst intervals (IBIs) are a key characteristic of discontinuity, yet their definition does not easily translate to AI detection. Objectives: To introduce low-voltage intervals (LVIs), defined exclusively by amplitude and duration, as a context-independent alternative to IBIs, develop an AI detection method for LVIs, and assess their clinical utility as a marker of brain injury. Methods: We developed a ConvNeXt model to detect LVIs and compared its performance with existing methods. We then tested the clinical relevance of detected LVIs across four applications: 1) grading background EEG abnormalities on an open benchmark dataset, 2) classifying clinical hypoxic-ischaemic encephalopathy (HIE) grades and comparing with a normal EEG dataset, 3) seizure prediction, and 4) association with seizure burden. Results: For training and validation, 654 hours of per-channel EEG from 123 neonates were reviewed and 51,162 LVIs were annotated. On held-out validation, ConvNeXt had an AUC of 0.996 and a Matthews correlation coefficient of 0.926. Model-reader agreement exceeded inter-reader agreement ($\Delta \kappa = 0.025$, 95% CI: 0.007 to 0.045, $p<0.001$), attaining expert-level equivalence. On a combined dataset of 444 neonates, percentage LVI showed a strong association with EEG grades (Spearman's $\rho=0.801$), a moderate association with HIE grades ($\rho=0.384$), a weaker association with seizure burden ($\rho=0.244$), and a strong seizure prediction capacity (AUC $=0.872$). Conclusion: AI detection of LVIs achieves expert-level equivalence, whereas quantitative features do not. Automated LVI quantification provides a robust clinical biomarker of neonatal encephalopathy associated with background EEG activity, HIE severity, and seizure risk.

papers.title: Inverse Synthesis of Shock Time Series from Shock Response Spectra Using Ensembles of Conditional Variational Autoencoders
papers.abstract: The shock response spectrum (SRS) characterizes the peak responses of single-degree-of-freedom systems to transient acceleration. Because the mapping from an acceleration time series (waveform) to its SRS is many-to-one, inverse synthesis seeks candidate waveforms consistent with a prescribed spectrum. We extend an earlier conditional variational autoencoder (CVAE) framework with a recurrent decoder that predicts multiscale wavelet coefficients and reconstructs waveforms through an inverse discrete wavelet transform. Individual models exhibit limited variability under latent sampling, motivating an ensemble of independently trained models spanning different mother wavelets and decomposition levels. Each member produces a separate candidate waveform for the same target SRS. Evaluation on four held-out benchmark datasets shows lower mean and median spectral errors for the illustrated wavelet model than for the earlier direct time-domain CVAE and a sum-of-decayed-sinusoids (SDS) baseline. A conditioning study examines frequency-grid and encoding choices. Comparisons with published inverse-SRS methods demonstrate superior performance across four holdout benchmark datasets (two operational shock datasets, one earthquake dataset, and one synthetic shock dataset) and competitive performance on synthetic targets reported by Brake. Single-model inference requires approximately 0.1-0.6 ms per waveform during batched inference compared with 5-8 s for SDS, excluding offline training. This low inference cost enables rapid generation of distinct SRS-compatible candidate waveforms across the ensemble, although their physical suitability requires assessment beyond spectral agreement.

papers.title: EarLog: Opportunistic Ear Physiology Sensing toward Personalized Hearing Risk Awareness
papers.abstract: Many headphone users risk irreversible hearing damage during high-load listening, yet current protection still relies on sound-pressure limits. Clinical tests detect damage after it becomes measurable, leaving the risk-accumulating process unobserved. The acoustic reflex (AR), an involuntary response to high acoustic load, marks when the ear enters a protective state. AR traces are weak, and existing measurements require dedicated probes and controlled conditions that are difficult to maintain during everyday audio. We present EarLog, which turns playback, the dominant interference, into an opportunistic probe. EarLog introduces content-conditioned residual sensing to suppress variations caused by nonstationary content, individual ear acoustics, and device response. It identifies weak AR through loudness-dependent changes and localized spectral irregularities in the residual. A resonance-constrained sparse finite impulse response (FIR) model captures the short-window response. Dual-microphone observations, mild-distortion recovery, and cross-session reference updates keep detection usable under low signal-to-noise ratio (SNR), fit changes, and environmental drift. EarLog runs in real time on an embedded controller using a low-cost dual-microphone add-on. We evaluate it with 81 participants, 16 headphone models, and more than 400 hours of recordings. EarLog achieves 99.0% sensitivity and 98.7% specificity on a clinically referenced benchmark. EarLog records listener-specific AR events during everyday listening, providing data for future longitudinal studies of hearing risk.

papers.title: Lightweight Time-Frequency Vibration Sensing for Consumer Device Condition Monitoring
papers.abstract: Consumer rotating devices, including washing machines, air conditioners, electric fans, robotic vacuum cleaners, and home fitness equipment, increasingly rely on vibration sensing for intelligent condition monitoring and predictive maintenance. Ensuring reliable operation in these resource-constrained appliances requires efficient, lightweight artificial intelligence (AI) solutions capable of processing non-stationary signals under real-world operational interference. This paper proposes a lightweight AI-assisted vibration sensing framework that employs continuous wavelet transform (CWT) and Hilbert-Huang transform (HHT) to convert one-dimensional (1-D) vibration time-series signals into two-dimensional (2-D) time-frequency representations. These representations are subsequently analyzed using lightweight deep learning architectures, specifically MobileNetV3-Small, ConvNeXt-Tiny, and the You Only Look Once version 11 classification model (YOLOv11-cls). Public bearing benchmark datasets, including Case Western Reserve University (CWRU), Paderborn University (PU), and Intelligent Maintenance Systems (IMS), are utilized as representative rotating components to investigate model generalization. The proposed framework is designed with eventual embedded deployment in consumer electronics in mind. Experimental results demonstrate that CWT combined with YOLOv11-cls achieves high diagnostic accuracy, while MobileNetV3-Small provides an attractive low-latency alternative for computationally constrained edge platforms. Conventional random splitting is also compared with dataset-specific structured isolation. The results highlight the importance of avoiding data leakage and quantify tradeoffs in classification accuracy, parameter count, floating-point operations (FLOPs), model footprint, preprocessing cost, and central processing unit (CPU) inference latency.

papers.title: Certified Outage Dimensioning of Fluid Antenna Receivers: Required SNR, Aperture, and Port Count
papers.abstract: We study the SNR, aperture, and port count needed to meet a target outage in a single-user downlink with a fixed transmit antenna and a single-RF fluid antenna receiver. For known spatially correlated Rayleigh channels and ideal port selection, a sampling-free residual certificate controls reduced-rank outage error over a continuous SNR interval. Positive Bessel features support large arrays, and bounded importance sampling converts the certificate into simultaneous design intervals. At 1 bit/s/Hz and outage $10^{-5}$, a four-wavelength, ten-port receiver requires 4.40--4.55 dB. Reducing its port count from 256 to ten costs 0.70--1.25 dB under a joint 95\% probability statement. At 3.5 wavelengths, ten ports require 4.90--5.05 dB. Integer-port screening across 3--8 dB shows how aperture and port requirements change with available SNR; an effective-SNR transformation extends these decisions to other rates. The reported intervals include model and sampling uncertainty under checked Gaussian covariance inputs. A constructive slow-growth rank bound and a 16--1024-port study support compact evaluation as port count grows.

papers.title: JEPA-kMMVAE: CSI Prediction for Time-Varying Wireless Channels
papers.abstract: This paper considers channel state information (CSI) prediction using neural networks for time-varying multi-antenna channels from noisy historical observations. The main challenge is to exploit temporal correlation while distinguishing channel evolution from observation noise. We propose JEPA-kMMVAE, which combines a joint-embedding predictive architecture with a k-memory Markov variational autoencoder to predict future CSI through temporally structured latent representations. The framework supports direct prediction and residual corrections relative to the latest latent state and noisy CSI observation. Simulation results show that the residual configuration outperforms the evaluated baselines at moderate and high input CSI signal-to-noise ratios, while sequence baselines remain more accurate under stronger noise.

papers.title: Tri-Hybrid SWIPT with Reconfigurable Parasitic Antennas
papers.abstract: We propose a coupling-aware tri-hybrid precoding architecture for simultaneous wireless information and power transfer (SWIPT) using reconfigurable parasitic antennas. By integrating multiport network theory and information theory, we develop a third precoding layer that explicitly accounts for mutual coupling and reactive energy storage within the antenna domain. To efficiently optimize this architecture, we propose a low-complexity tri-hybrid solution comprising coordinate descent (CD) for parasitic reactive load optimization, a singular value decomposition (SVD)-based analog precoder, and a protective partial zero-forcing (PPZF) digital precoder. Numerical results demonstrate that the transmit array introduces impedance mismatch that reduces the real power accepted by the antenna array. Moreover, the proposed tri-hybrid architecture significantly outperforms hybrid precoding by constructively exploiting the coupling effects, yielding substantial gains in spectral efficiency (SE) and sum non-linear harvested energy (NLHE) at a fraction of the hardware cost.

papers.title: One Thing Leads to Another: The Essentials of Time Series Causal Discovery
papers.abstract: Time series causal discovery --- the process of detecting causation between time series --- has its roots in signal processing research from over a half century ago. It has since received active and widespread interest, evolving into different forms across domains such as statistics, dynamical systems and machine learning. Entering this fragmented and constantly evolving research landscape can be daunting. This tutorial provides a unified overview of time series causal discovery across research communities. We introduce the key principles invoked by modern discovery methods, and we discuss their limitations and assumptions. We also discuss how discovery methods are evaluated, benchmarked and fine-tuned. We further discuss how causal discovery for time series is becoming crucial for downstream tasks in agriculture and Earth science, in healthcare, and in artificial intelligence systems. We believe that this tutorial will serve as a valuable resource in navigating the deluge of recent causality research, as well as an invitation to signal processing audiences to contribute to causal problems. To further help readers, we host a companion repository to link to useful code packages and resources at https://github.com/CHAI-UK/Awesome-Time-Series-Causal-Discovery.

papers.title: On the Performance of Randomly Generated Codebooks in Near-Field Communications
papers.abstract: Near-field communication with large antenna arrays requires beamforming techniques that account for spherical wavefront effects. While predefined codebooks are widely used in multiple-antenna wireless systems, the performance of randomly generated codebooks in the near-field region has not been investigated. In this work, we study four randomly generated codebooks for near-field communications: random vector quantization (RVQ), random phase (RP), random far-field (RFF), and random near-field (RNF) codebooks. We use the known RVQ gain distribution as a benchmark. For RP, we derive a large-array bulk approximation and characterize the high-gain tail behavior of the gain distribution. For RNF, we characterize the high-gain tail behavior of the gain distribution. For RFF, we derive an analytical approximation for the maximum achievable beamforming gain when far-field beams are used to serve near-field users, along with the corresponding maximizing far-field direction. We also analyze the maximum-gain scaling with codebook size. Monte Carlo simulations verify the analytical results and show that RVQ and RP degrade significantly as the array size increases, while RNF achieves the most favorable high-gain scaling. RFF can outperform RVQ and RP for finite codebook sizes, but its maximum gain saturates below one due to the phase mismatch between the far-field beams and the near-field channel. These results show how codebook structure, array size, and codebook size affect random beamforming performance in the near-field.

papers.title: Simultaneous Direct and Indirect Channel Estimation for RIS-Assisted MIMO Communications
papers.abstract: This paper introduces an enhanced channel estimation method for reconfigurable intelligent surface (RIS)-assisted multiple-input multiple-output (MIMO) communications. Considering the presence of both the direct link from the base station (BS) to the user equipment (UE) and the indirect link \textit{via} the RIS, we formulate a tensor-based receiver for joint direct and indirect channel estimation called the TenDICE algorithm. The proposed receiver relies on an extended parallel factor analysis (PARAFAC) tensor model for the received pilot signals, from which the involved (direct and indirect link) channels are estimated using a simple alternating least squares scheme. The proposed TenDICE method is compared with the state-of-the-art least squares (LS) method, Khatri-Rao factorization (KRF) method, enhanced trilinear alternating least squares (E-TALS), and the theoretical Cram\'er-Rao lower bound (CRLB) based on normalized mean square error (NMSE) and spectral efficiency (SE). The proposed TenDICE outperforms the LS and E-TALS methods and performs similarly to the KRF methods while estimating the direct channel.

papers.title: Low-Complexity Tensor-Based Channel Parameter Estimation for mmWave MIMO-Assisted Systems
papers.abstract: This paper presents a low-complexity tensor-based channel estimation framework for downlink mmWave massive MIMO systems using passive Butler-matrix beamforming. By modeling received signals as a third-order PARAFAC tensor, we exploit known pilot structures via bilinear alternating least-squares (BALS) optimization to reduce computational overhead. The decoupled spatial factors are then processed via 1D and 2D ESPRIT to extract angles of arrival and departure with automatic pairing. Additionally, we derive the Cramer--Rao lower bound (CRLB) for this architecture. Simulations confirm the proposed estimator outperforms conventional least-squares, achieving accurate channel reconstruction and approaching the CRLB at moderate-to-high signal-to-noise ratios.

papers.title: Multistatic Terahertz ISAC for Object Shape Identification
papers.abstract: 6G networks are expected to sense their surroundings using the same waveforms that carry data. We ask how much can be learned about the shape of an object from the terahertz echoes that user equipment transmissions produce as they scatter from that object on their way to a ceiling-mounted access point, with no sensing hardware beyond the communication link itself. We build a physics-based multistatic forward model at a 300 GHz carrier with 50 GHz of bandwidth, combining Physical Optics (PO) and Physical Theory of Diffraction (PTD) scattering with an image-source multipath lattice, molecular absorption and directional horn antennas. The model makes explicit a property of the PO mechanism hierarchy that is usually left implicit. Six physically distinct mechanisms share only three frequency exponents, so the spectral slope does not by itself determine which mechanisms a target presents and therefore cannot by itself determine its geometry. Angular diversity is accordingly a requirement for identifiability rather than an optional refinement. We compare a transmitter-count-invariant 2D-CNN with a physics-informed RBF-SVM on object orientations never seen in training. Accuracy climbs from roughly 70 percent with one transmitter to 96-97 percent with 20. The CNN gains in two regimes, irregular placement and lossy targets, while on metal under quasi-uniform placement the SVM baseline is fully competitive. Performance falls off gradually under occlusion, holding 78 percent with three quarters of the surface hidden and 63 percent when the classifier has never seen an occluded target. Multi-object scenes are limited by interference between overlapping returns rather than by angular coverage, so presence detection saturates after roughly four transmitters.

papers.title: Generative Control of Time-Modulated Intelligent Reflecting Surfaces for Scalable Directional Modulation
papers.abstract: Time-modulated intelligent reflecting surfaces (TM-IRS) achieve directional modulation by switching their elements on and off at designed instants and durations, so that an undistorted signal reaches the intended user while appearing scrambled elsewhere. We propose a Flow Matching (FM)-based generative framework that designs these parameters for strong scrambling and reliable reception simultaneously. For orthogonal frequency-division multiplexing (OFDM) signals, we introduce a physics-informed reward that maximizes the time-modulation harmonic energy radiated in the null space of the legitimate-user response, subject to a minimum per-subcarrier signal-to-interference-plus-noise ratio (SINR), without requiring knowledge of adversary directions. Unlike prior generative flow network (GFlowNet) approaches, which assign discretized parameters sequentially, the FM model generates complete continuous configurations jointly, decoupling the generation depth from the number of elements and accelerating training. It also learns a distribution over configurations that can be resampled to vary the scrambling pattern. Numerical results show that, compared with a GFlowNet baseline, the proposed approach reduces the time to training loss near-saturation by $99.4\%$ on average for $3{\times}3$ to $12{\times}12$ surfaces, attains higher final rewards, scales to $80{\times}80$, and confines the low-symbol-error region more tightly around the legitimate user.

papers.title: Self-Calibration DOA Estimation for Moving Dilated Arrays with Gain and Phase Errors
papers.abstract: Moving dilated arrays (MDAs) can increase the uniform degrees of freedom (uDOFs) while alleviating mutual coupling, but their performance is susceptible to unknown gain and phase errors (GPEs). To deal with this problem, we investigate self-calibration direction-of-arrival (DOA) estimation for MDAs with unknown GPEs. First, multi-position observations are phase aligned to construct an equivalent virtual array with an enlarged aperture. Next, the motion-induced relationships among the GPEs are exploited to establish explicit calibration constraints. By leveraging the orthogonality between the steering vectors and the noise subspace, the joint estimation of the DOAs and GPEs is formulated as a constrained optimization problem. To solve this problem, a two-stage alternating optimization (AO) algorithm is developed. In the first stage, the GPEs are estimated in closed form with the DOAs fixed. In the second stage, the estimated GPEs are used to calibrate the covariance matrix, after which the DOAs are refined using the multiple signal classification (MUSIC) algorithm. To obtain reliable initial estimates, a rotational invariance-like (RIL) initialization method is further developed by exploiting two translated virtual subarrays with identical GPEs. Furthermore, the Cramer-Rao bound (CRB) is derived to characterize the theoretical performance limit of the considered system. Simulation results demonstrate that the proposed method converges reliably and achieves accurate DOA estimation under different array apertures, numbers of snapshots, GPE levels, and numbers of sources.

papers.title: LLM-Assisted Hierarchical Interference Control for Satellite-Terrestrial Integrated Networks
papers.abstract: Time-varying aggregate interference from low-Earth-orbit (LEO) satellites challenges terrestrial-network (TN) protection, whereas conservative control degrades LEO quality of service (QoS). This letter proposes a hierarchical framework combining geometry-based interference estimation, QoS-constrained power control, adaptive energy detection, large language model (LLM)-assisted candidate ranking, stay-or-switch decisions, and target-band selection, with deterministic verification. The current band is retained only when both spectrum-hole and power-feasibility conditions hold, with periodic reevaluation. Over a 300-s horizon with 0.5-s sampling, the proposed method keeps the aggregate INR from exceeding the $-12.2$~dB threshold and achieves a time-averaged mean LEO-link rate of $320.97$~Mbps with $100\%$ QoS satisfaction. It markedly outperforms power-only and satellite-muting in jointly protecting the TN and preserving LEO QoS.

papers.title: Towards Signal Processing In Networks: Multiplierless Block Transforms in Data Plane
papers.abstract: In this paper, we propose a signal processing concept, signal processing in networks (SPIN), that executes signal processing tasks directly on programmable switches. Traditionally, signal processing tasks, such as denoising, decomposition, and dimensionality reduction, are performed on edge or cloud servers, i.e., raw streams are transmitted from sensors. This imposes a heavy processing load on edge/cloud servers and requires substantial bandwidth. SPIN addresses this problem by performing signal processing on the forwarding path. As an initial realization of SPIN, we implement a DCT-based block transform on a programmable switch. We redesign its computation using a lifting-based lattice structure, multiplierless approximation, and pipeline partitioning across stages in a programmable switch. We verify at the compiler level that the proposed implementation satisfies the strict hardware constraints of the Intel Tofino2--specifically regarding pipeline stages, packet header vector, and ternary content-addressable memory usage--and therefore enables line-rate processing. We further quantify the per-packet latency of the ingress match-action pipeline. The SPIN-oriented preprocessing adds 46 cycles (approximately 31 ns at 1.5 GHz). The total ingress match-action unit latency is approximately 87 ns, which remains consistent with the low-latency operation targeted by SPIN. Furthermore, we implement the proposed block transform on a BMv2 switch using P4 and evaluate it as preprocessing for in-network machine learning. Experimental results demonstrate that the proposed method improves classification performance over unfiltered baselines.

papers.title: Scalable Quantum Clustering of Renewable Profiles via a Hybrid Qubit-efficient Strategy
papers.abstract: Large-scale renewable energy profile clustering is a computationally challenging NP-hard problem. Recent quantum computing techniques offer a potential remedy, yet their scalability is severely constrained by the limited qubit count of current quantum hardware. To address this issue, we first cast the problem into a QUBO form and then we propose a consensus-based variable reduction (CBVR) method to drastically cut qubit usage. More specifically, we tailor the one-hot constraint to eliminate assignment variables and leverage consensus analysis to convert stable clustering relations from initial anneals into equality constraints for further reduction. Experiments on real quantum hardware confirm that CBVR compresses oversized QUBO models into feasible sizes while retaining high clustering quality and efficiency.

papers.title: Blind and Asynchronous Initial Beam Acquisition and Clock-Assisted Re-Acquisition in Standalone Mobile MIMO-OFDM Systems
papers.abstract: Building upon our preliminary study, this paper proposes a standalone beam-management framework for mobile MIMO-OFDM systems that integrates Blind Initial Beam Acquisition (BIBA) with Clock-Assisted Re-Acquisition (CARA). BIBA is a blind and asynchronous protocol that requires neither prior synchronization nor an out-of-band feedback channel, so the Base Station (BS) and User Equipment (UE) can independently identify the beam pair maximizing received signal strength. To handle subsequent link drops, the newly introduced CARA protocol exploits the clock synchronization established after BIBA to reduce the re-acquisition time by approximately 55% compared with BIBA. The operational reliability of both protocols is bounded by a probabilistic feasibility analysis under random UE mobility trajectories. Protocols are validated on a 28 GHz mmWave testbed under practical hardware constraints, including beam-switching and Time Division Duplex (TDD) latencies, and measured Software-Defined Radio (SDR) software processing delays. Finally, we formulate a unified Finite State Machine (FSM) model for both BIBA and CARA to ensure robust integration into practical wireless systems

papers.title: Suppressing Multiple GNSS Interferers with Local-Gradient Adaptive Notch Filtering
papers.abstract: Adaptive notch filters (ANFs) based on the normalized least mean squares (NLMS) algorithm are an established technique for suppressing narrowband interference in GNSS receivers. The traditional solution for multiple interferers is simply cascading the NLMS-ANF into multiple stages but this solution degrades performance when multiple chirp jammers of similar power are present. We propose a low-complexity modification to the cascaded NLMS-ANF update rule to resolve this: a local gradient (LG) formulation: LG-ANF. The LG-ANF forms a locally bandlimited gradient signal by translating the input to baseband around the current frequency estimate, low-pass filtering it, and translating it back, thereby attenuating competing interferers before adaptation. The modification generalizes the traditional NLMS-ANF to handle the similar-power multiple interferer problem, using just one additional parameter. We characterize the gradient-averaging failure analytically and visually, demonstrate independent chirp tracking in the worst-case two-chirp scenarios, and evaluate statistical suppression performance by sweeping amplitude ratio against a standard NLMS-ANF, a frequency-locked-loop (FLL)-based ANF and a per-sample oracle upper bound. We further characterize the LG advantage over various ANF parameters and chirp conditions. Simulations show that the LG-ANF reduces to the standard NLMS-ANF outside the pathological multi-chirp regime, while recovering up to 4dB of in-band suppression around pathological amplitude ratios under per-condition optimization of the local bandwidth, and up to 13dB for selected edge-case parameter combinations. These optimized results represent an upper bound on the achievable LG gain. In a hardware experiment using a fixed alpha_lp=0.5, the LG-ANF extends position-lock survival by 24s relative to the standard ANF.

papers.title: HF Single-Station Localization via Multimode Ray Tracing and Time-Frequency Information Fusion
papers.abstract: High-frequency (HF) single-station localization estimates an emitter location from measured directions of arrival (DOAs) and an ionospheric propagation model. When the propagation mode composition cannot be identified from conventional direction-finding (DF) measurements, the same DF observation may produce multiple physically valid ground landing points under different propagation modes, making the location inversion ambiguous. This paper proposes a multimode time-frequency information fusion localization method (MTFIF-L).Rather than assuming a propagation mode a priori, MTFIF-L retains valid landing points generated under different propagation modes and uses repeated observations across time windows and, when available, multiple operating frequencies to progressively constrain the resulting candidate locations. Experiments on four measured HF links examine the respective roles of multimode candidate retention, cross-window processing, and cross-frequency processing. All four links yield unique location decisions. Links A--C achieve relative errors of $1.40\%$, $0.78\%$, and $3.41\%$, respectively.Link D, the only single-frequency case, also yields a unique decision from repeated temporal observations, although its post- localization error is substantially larger. Propagation-path analysis further reveals link-dependent differences in reflection layer, hop count, magnetoionic mode, and elevation angle among the ray-tracing paths associated with the measured links.Overall, the results show that repeated temporal observations can support localization within an individual frequency, while multifrequency information provides additional robustness against unreliable frequency-specific outcomes, enabling HF single-station localization under unknown and potentially coexisting propagation modes while retaining interpretable propagation information for post-localization analysis.

papers.title: OpenH-RF: A Large-Scale Ultrasound Raw Channel Dataset Initiative
papers.abstract: Medical ultrasound is a widely accessible, real-time imaging modality, yet progress in data-driven ultrasound research is constrained by the scarcity of large, open collections of raw channel data. Existing public datasets are predominantly based on reconstructed images, while the smaller number of open raw channel datasets is generally specialized to individual reconstruction or imaging tasks, limiting the development of general-purpose methods and foundation models that operate directly on ultrasound signals. While interpretive tasks can be performed on reconstructed images, many of the key technical challenges in ultrasound imaging, such as aberration correction and reverberation reduction, require the raw channel data itself. We introduce OpenH-RF, a community-driven open dataset initiative comprising approximately 40 TB of medical ultrasound raw channel data in 19,332 acquisitions, contributed by 38 institutions across academia and industry, spanning in-vivo, phantom, and simulated data. Each dataset is annotated with a number of supported tasks, ranging from generalized reconstruction, speed-of-sound estimation, and aberration correction to blood flow imaging, motion estimation, quantitative ultrasound, and image interpretation. OpenH-RF provides a unified, self-contained data format that captures raw channel data together with the acquisition, probe, metadata, and reconstruction information required for reproducible processing across scanners and acquisition schemes. The corpus is publicly hosted under a permissive CC BY 4.0 license and can be streamed programmatically and selectively at scale. By bringing heterogeneous ultrasound data into a common representation, backed by modern data infrastructure, OpenH-RF lowers the barrier to working with raw channel data and aims to open medical ultrasound research to new communities. See https://open-h.github.io/OpenH-RF.

papers.title: SEER: Source-Conditioned Emotion Enhancement via Retrieval for Cochlear-Implant Speech
papers.abstract: Cochlear implants (CIs) restore speech access but weaken cues needed for vocal emotion recognition. Prior CI-oriented enhancement requires parallel normal/strong recordings and intensity labels. We propose SEER, a retrieval-based framework that learns which same-emotion reference helps each source remain recognizable after CI processing. A source-conditioned retriever learns CI-aware utility from sampled emotional voice conversion outcomes, while uncertainty-guided exploration avoids exhaustive pair evaluation; neither parallel recordings nor intensity labels are required. SEER improves Source macro-F1 at N8 by 7.30 points on RAVDESS and 11.66 points on ESD, with significant ESD gains across N4/N8/N16. Sixteen-listener RAVDESS gains are significant across all conditions. Exhaustive analysis finds an aggregate benefit from stronger references but little effect from matching gender or content.

papers.title: Zeros of the Spectrogram of White Noise with Hermite Windows
papers.abstract: We study the zeros of the spectrogram of complex white noise analyzed with Hermite windows of order n, extending the classical Gaussian-window correspondence with Gaussian Analytic Functions to the polyanalytic setting. Using the polyanalytic Bargmann transform, these zeros split into two families according to the sign of the local Jacobian, giving rise to a natural notion of charge, and we show that these zeros are almost surely simple, isolated, and form a translation and rotation-invariant point process. We derive closed-form expressions for the one-point intensity, decomposed by charge, and also for the unsigned, signed, and hybrid two-point intensities. Besides, we prove that unlike the total repulsion observed with a Gaussian window, the Hermite window of order n generates a pair correlation function that converges at the origin to a strictly positive constant depending on n. Finally, we propose a numerical method for detecting spectrogram zeros via the winding number around candidate local minima.
